concept: Cache stampede protection: leases, request coalescing, TTL jitter
summary: Source-anchored research for Cache stampede protection: leases, request coalescing, TTL jitter. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Application guidance for read offload: coordinate the expensive refill per logical result (for example with a lock keyed on the cache key so one request rebuilds while others wait), add random jitter to TTLs so entries written together do not expire together, and decide whether stale results are acceptable while refresh runs (stale-while-revalidate is appropriate only where a stale read is not a correctness problem). This is generic cache-layer guidance from caching sources, not a built-in MongoDB stampede guarantee. Sources: https://redisson.pro/glossary/thundering-herd-problem.html

A cache-refill lease can combine authorization to populate a key with throttling of refill attempts. Facebook's design binds a token to the requested key, checks it on refill, and invalidates it when a delete arrives, preventing an obsolete fill from being accepted. (low confidence)
Refreshing every request inside a fixed early-refresh window can merely move the stampede earlier. Early refresh still needs a mechanism that limits concurrent origin work. (low confidence)

A hot cache entry can cause concurrent backend recomputation when it expires. Longer recomputation leaves more time for duplicate misses, and the resulting load can slow recomputation further. (high confidence)

In probabilistic early expiration, each request may regenerate the item before its expiration by making an independent probabilistic decision, which mitigates the stampede. The approach has no guarantees for its effectiveness. Sources: https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~avattani/papers/cache_stampede.pdf

Lock-based refresh needs a follower policy: callers can wait for regeneration or use a retained stale value when the application permits it. Without a usable value, callers need an explicit absence or failure path. (medium confidence)

Refresh locks need a suitably chosen expiry (high enough to recompute the item) and failure handling. If the lock owner fails while regenerating, no item or a stale item is served until the lock expires and a new lock is acquired. Sources: https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~avattani/papers/cache_stampede.pdf

Go singleflight.Group.Do ensures only one execution is in flight for a given key at a time within that Group; duplicate callers wait for the original and receive the same results. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sync/singleflight

Random TTL jitter spreads expiration times across keys and reduces synchronized backend refill load. It complements per-key coalescing: choosing a random expiry for one shared key does not itself serialize that key's concurrent misses. The latter conclusion follows from the mechanisms' different scopes. (medium confidence) Sources: https://codemia.io/archive/cache-stampede-protection ; https://system-design.space/en/labs/cache-stampede-hot-key-ttl/

Facebook's 2013 implementation rate-limited lease-token issuance per key and told other callers to wait briefly. Treat this as a historical implementation example, not a universal lease-duration recommendation. (low confidence)

Non-leading requests need an explicit response policy: wait for regeneration, return an acceptable stale value, or handle the missing value. A failed lock holder can leave readers waiting or using stale data until the lock expires. (high confidence)

The lock's time-to-live must be high enough to recompute the item. The locking approach is not fault-tolerant: if the request holding the lock fails while regenerating the item, no item or a stale item is served until the lock expires and a new lock is acquired. Sources: https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~avattani/papers/cache_stampede.pdf
Per-key request coalescing allows one in-flight computation and shares its result with concurrent callers, reducing duplicate origin work within the coordinator's scope. (high confidence)

Facebook's 2013 memcache design issues a key-bound lease token on a miss and validates that token on cache fill. A delete invalidates the token, preventing an obsolete fill. Rate-limiting lease issuance also reduces simultaneous database fetches while other clients wait and retry. These are properties of that design, not guarantees of every Memcached deployment. (low confidence)

Probabilistic early refresh lets requests independently decide to regenerate before expiry, with refresh probability increasing near expiration. This avoids a shared lock but provides no deterministic guarantee of exactly one origin request. (medium confidence)
